function.name: ProductSearch_execute
function.description: Performs a search for products in the database based on specified criteria, such as keywords and filters, and returns a list of matching products. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

keywords.description: The search terms used to find products, separated by spaces.

category.description: The category to filter the search results. If no category is specified, all categories will be included in the search.

price_range.description: A price range to narrow down the search results, specified as a string in the format 'min-max' where min and max are prices in USD.

sort_order.description: The order in which the search results are sorted. Choose 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

in_stock.description: A flag to filter search results to only include products that are in stock. Set to true to include only in-stock items.

message.content:
Hai! 😊  
Saat ini saya belum punya akses ke sistem inventaris sehingga nggak bisa kasih tahu pasti kapan produk berwarna **pink** akan di‑restock lagi.  

Berikut beberapa cara yang biasanya membantu:

| Cara | Keterangan |
|------|------------|
| **Cek ulang situs/APP** | Kadang stok muncul setelah update otomatis. |
| **Daftar email pemberitahuan** | Banyak toko menawarkan “notifikasi restock” lewat email atau push notification. |
| **Hubungi customer service** | Bisa langsung tanya nomor kontak / chat resmi mereka untuk info terbaru. |

Jika kamu mau, beri tahu nama produk spesifiknya (misalnya “Kaos Pink X”) dan kategori (baju, aksesoris, dll.)—mungkin aku dapat bantu cari apakah ada varian lain yang masih tersedia. Kalau tidak, sebaiknya cek kembali nanti atau minta bantuan tim penjualan. 

Semoga cepat dapet barang favoritmu! 🚀

But we can't answer without data. Maybe we should politely say we cannot determine restocking time currently. Or we could try searching for "pink" across categories. Use ProductSearch_execute with keywords="pink" and sort_order=asc etc. That may return something. Then we can infer availability. But likely none found because no real DB.
